content:
**Dino Peaks Mini Golf** is a location in *Fallout 76*, introduced in the *Burning Springs* update.

A pre-war mini Golf Course, the Abraxodyne Chemical company began hiding their chemical waste on the premises, stashed inside the statues of the dinosaurs themselves. An investigative reporter attempted to find the hidden barrels, but was unable to locate them.

After the war, Charred Feral Ghouls have made this location their home, with Rusted Deathclaws nesting nearby.

| Image | Name | Description | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | Thunder from the Past | Known from limited fossil remains, Suuwassea were a smaller, more mysterious member of the long-necked dinosaur family. They likely traveled in groups and fed from treetops in what is now the American West. Though not as large as their cousins, Suuwassea fossils showcase the diverse life found in the Morrison Formation of the Late Jurassic Period. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | The Sharpest Mind of the Mesozoic | Small in size but big in brainpower, Troodon are one of the most intelligent dinosaurs ever discovered. With large forward-facing eyes, grasping hands, and a brain-to-body ratio closer to modern birds than reptiles, Troodon were likely quick thinkers and clever hunters. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | The Plated Defender | Stegosaurus are one of the most iconic dinosaurs of all time. Instantly recognizable by the bony plates running down their backs and the fearsome spikes on their tails. Living in the Late Jurassic period, Stegosaurus were slow-moving herbivores that relied on their armor for protection. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | Built to Endure | Often overlooked in favor of flashier dinosaurs, Tenontosaurus were true survivors. These medium-sized herbivores lived through a period of major ecological change during the Early Cretaceous. Strong limbs, a stiff tail, and a low center of gravity helped Tenontosaurs navigate rough terrain and avoid danger. Healed injuries on some fossils suggest they could survive attacks from predators like Deinonychus or Saurornitholestes. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | The Ghost of the Eastern Shore | Appalachiosaurus were swift, bipedal predators that patrolled the dense, humid lowlands of what is now the eastern United States. Named for the ancient landmass of Appalachia, these dinosaurs highlight the regional diversity of prehistoric life. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | The Three-Horned Titan | One of the last great dinosaurs to roam North America, Triceratops were heavily built herbivores with three formidable horns and frilled skulls. Weighing up to 12 tons, Triceratops used their bulk and horns for defence. Some fossils even bear healed bite marks; evidence they were able to survive deadly encounters with the predators like the Tyrannosaurus rex. | 
| [[File:\|180px]] | Alamosaurus Info | After a long absence in the fossil record, massive sauropods like Alamosaurus returned to roam North America in the Late Cretaceous. Towering and tenacious, they stood as living proof that giants could walk the Earth once more. These giants could reach lengths over 60 feet and likely traveled in herds for safety. | 

Dino Peaks Mini Golf appears in *Fallout 76*.
